A cyberattack happens every 39 seconds.  3.4 billion phishing emails are sent every day. Someone becomes an identity theft victim every 4.9 seconds. And 22% of Americans will experience identity theft in their lifetime.  A cybersecurity analyst who's worked in incident response for 12 years told me: "People think hackers target celebrities, corporations, and governments. They don't. They target the person who reused their Gmail password on a fitness app that got breached in 2021."  "80% of people use the same password across multiple accounts. 70% don't use two-factor authentication. 86% have never changed their router's admin password. And almost nobody has checked if their email is already in a breach database  even though it's free and takes 10 seconds."  "The average identity theft victim loses $500  but 125,000 people last year lost over $10,000 each. And every single one of them could have prevented it with settings that were already on their phone."  "Your phone has a SIM lock, your email has 2FA, your credit bureau has a free freeze, and your browser has a breach checker. All free. All sitting there. All turned off." 9:00 a.m. A phishing email gets quarantined. 9:05 a.m. An endpoint runs a suspicious PowerShell command.  Each one looks handled on its own. The quarantine did its job, and one odd PowerShell process a day is background noise in most environments.  Together they're the opening moves of a campaign. Nobody sees them side by side because they live in 2 different tools.  Sublime Security's email telemetry now lands natively in Elastic Security, next to your endpoint, identity, and network data.  From there, Attack Discovery ties the quarantined email to the endpoint alerts and builds one attack chain. Mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, reasoning included.  Elastic Workflows opens a case and pings the analyst on Slack, evidence attached. Approve or reject from there.  The agents connect the signals and surface an evidence-backed decision. Consequential actions still go through the analyst.  Full walkthrough, including the 7-step flow and the two-stage rollout: go.es.io/4hHaGka

The Gentlemen have been anything but, and after working through the public reporting from Microsoft, Check Point, Group-IB, Huntress, Trend Micro and others, I pulled everything into one full threat actor profile so defenders have it all in one place.  This RaaS operation, tracked by Microsoft as Storm-2697, grew out of Qilin affiliate activity in mid-2025 and has already posted more than 320 victims in 2026, hitting healthcare, education, manufacturing, transportation and financial services. Their favorite way in is still an unpatched edge device, with Fortinet CVE-2024-55591 at the top of the list and a database of roughly 14,700 FortiGates to work through, and once inside they kill EDR with vulnerable signed drivers and push the encryptor across the whole domain through Group Policy, which means an entire environment can go down in a matter of hours.  The part that should get every business owner's attention is that these operators aren't picking victims because they're careless - they're picking the ones that are busy and missed one patch on one appliance. In one negotiation exposed in the group's own leaked data, they opened at $250,000 and settled at $190,000.  In the full profile you'll find: - How a Gentlemen intrusion unfolds, from initial access all the way to impact - Six CISA KEV-listed CVEs to put at the top of your patch list - A full MITRE ATT&CK mapping - IOCs along with practical detection and hunting guidance - A plan to close the doors they use, watch for the moves they make, and rehearse the day it happens  If you run Fortinet, VMware ESXi or Veeam anywhere in your environment, you'll want to check this out.  Read it here - na2.hubs.ly/H084NXC0 #ransomware #threatintel #dfir #incidentresponse #cybersecurity

CVE-2026-73570: Unauthenticated OS command injection in Zimbra Collaboration Suite's SNMP notification path is actively exploited in the wild, listed in CISA KEV, and delivers full mail-store access, credential theft, and persistent remote-access implants.  Key findings:  - The vulnerability lives in the swatchdog-to-snmptrap execution path. A crafted SMTP request injects shell metacharacters into SNMP notification processing, executing as the zimbra service account with no authentication required. Exploitation requires the optional zimbra-snmp package installed and SNMP notifications enabled. Patch to Zimbra 10.1.20 (released July 20, 2026) immediately. If patching must wait, uninstall zimbra-snmp, disable SNMP notifications, and restrict SMTP and SNMP access to trusted hosts only. Microsoft telemetry captured active exploitation between the patch release and public disclosure on August 13, 2026, meaning attackers operated with knowledge of the vulnerability before defenders had a CVE to work from. The MITRE ATT&CK techniques observed span T1595.002, T1190, T1059.004, T1105, T1068, T1053.003, T1543.002, T1505.003, T1036.005, T1620, T1083, T1071.001, T1102.001, T1560.001, T1074.001, and T1496.  - The post-exploitation chain is deep and deliberate. After initial access, attackers deployed multiple JSP webshells into Jetty and mailboxd application paths and propagated them via the existing zimbra SSH identity at /opt/zimbra/.ssh/zimbra_identity and rsync to peer mailbox nodes. Privilege escalation abused the interaction between zmmailboxdmgr, its writable log directory, pam_exec, and zmstat-fd to make /etc/pam.d/sudo writable by the zimbra account, then added a NOPASSWD: ALL sudoers entry. The sudoers file was written to /etc/sudoers.d/81_metric. A persistence service named zimlog.service was dropped into /etc/systemd/system/ and timestomped to match the modification times of rsync.service and sshd.service. Memory-backed execution used memfd_create via /proc/self/fd. C2 included an OpenSSL reverse shell over a named pipe at /tmp/s and a zimclient2 WebSocket agent at psk1zim.abrdns[.]com/agentws with TLS and raw TCP fallbacks. One campaign stage polled encrypted commands from a Base blockchain contract at 0x25bdA7Feb3553995AD68a9A8Ed8c731b73a71586 over public JSON-RPC.  - Credential and mailbox collection was purpose-built. A Go binary with embedded module path zimbra-exfil/client-dump reads /opt/zimbra/conf/localconfig.xml and extracts mysql_root_password, zimbra_mysql_password, ldap_root_password, and six additional LDAP service credentials, then exports full contents from the mailbox, mailbox_metadata, mobile_devices, and out_of_office tables plus all zimbra.* namespace tables. A separate dumpSecrets function retrieves zimbraAuthTokenKey from cn=config,cn=zimbra, which enables forging valid session tokens for any account without credentials, and zimbraPreAuthKey, which enables pre-authenticated login URL construction for any user. Collected material was staged under /tmp/zimbra_dump_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS/ and compressed. On one host, mail-store backup content was archived to /opt/zimbra/final.tar.gz and an AzCopy transfer was attempted to wsweb03.blob.core[.]windows[.]net/log/windows.log using an operator-supplied SAS URL. Transfer completion was not confirmed.  - The pre-disclosure reconnaissance window is a critical hunting interval. Between July 28 and August 7, two distinct scanning tools probed the injection path using the ZB73570 User-Agent and out-of-band callbacks to oast[.]fun, oast[.]online, dnslog.pp[.]ua, requestrepo[.]com, and bypass[.]eu[.]org subdomains. This activity predates the 30-day Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting retention window as of today. Defenders must search Sentinel or archived logs for the second-stage infrastructure. Key C2 IPs include 45.32.30[.]235:8081 and 8080, 193.42.40[.]135:443, and 3.209.137[.]175:443. Dropper domains include transzimbra.linkpc[.]net and wslogzimbra.linkpc[.]net. The S3-hosted dropper URL was mexico-cashpay-test.s3.dualstack.mx-central-1.amazonaws[.]com/pakistan/2026/aliyun_update.tar.gz. Key SHA-256 hashes include zimclient2 at b594a42b8f1c6f090327bb9a3361c2d3515537fb7ac8da6b9061b9a3f330e159 and zimdown2 at bf28f38122bf20d5fac969cc414daa6a890cdea872d389ca93d2092b6b7773cf.  Practitioner takeaway: On any confirmed Zimbra host, do not stop at quarantining a named payload. Several of the most consequential outcomes involved only a plain shell. Hunt for perl spawning sh or bash via a .swatchdog_script command line containing snmptrap and shell metacharacters. Check every mailbox node for unexpected JSP files and generated _jsp.java artifacts in jetty_base/webapps/, mailboxd/webapps/, and work/zimbra/jsp/. Inspect /etc/systemd/system/ for units with zimbra or logging names, unusual ownership, or timestamps matching sshd.service or rsync.service. Rotate zimbraPreAuthKey and zimbraAuthTokenKey immediately: possession of either value enables account takeover without credentials. Seven Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting queries covering the full attack chain, the full IOC list, and all named Defender detections are in the report.  #DFIR_Radar

The President addressed the plenary session of the 23rd annual meeting of the Valdai International Discussion Club.  Some parts of the speech is absolute masterpiece of bitter-ness (something I personally celebrate )...  This year's theme was "Responsibility for the Future: Limits of the Possible or Limitless Possibilities?"  Lukyanov's intro:   Dear friends! Distinguished guests!  I am pleased to welcome you to the plenary session of the 23rd Annual Meeting of the Valdai Discussion Club. It is my pleasure to invite the President of the Russian Federation, Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin, to the hall.  Vladimir Vladimirovich, welcome!  We are delighted that, just as in previous years, you have found the time and opportunity to meet with us.  The Valdai sessions are, of course, always intense. But, naturally, in keeping with what is happening in the world, this intensity and pace are growing, as is the mood—becoming increasingly elevated, so to speak.  This year, if one were to try to single out the core concepts of that session—of the forum that took place over the preceding three days—I would say that they are: change, for it is obvious we can all see that changes are occurring literally in every sphere of human activity; responsibility, because the more changes there are, the less clear understanding there is of future development, and the higher everyone's responsibility is toward that development; and the third concept, which might perhaps seem surprising—and we had rather intense discussions on this point as well—is the concept of calm ("Спокойствие")😎.    Our report, which we prepare annually, is titled 'Don’t Panic' 😎 this year. We suggest that under these complex circumstances, we avoid doing the most incorrect thing—which is to fret. I believe that from your vantage point, it is clearer which international concepts are currently the most vital, and therefore, I would be happy to invite you to speak.   The President:    Ladies and gentlemen! Colleagues!  Following a good tradition, we are gathering at the annual forum of the Valdai International Discussion Club to deliberate on the most pressing global issues.  Together, we have always strived not only to diagnose the state of the world but also to outline the contours of the emerging world order.  I am convinced that the intellectual wealth and the experience of direct, candid dialogue accumulated by the (Valdai) club will certainly be in demand when all of us—East and West, North and South—must sooner or later come to an agreement on the principles of forming a new world order capable of ensuring the progress and development of humanity for decades to come.  Regrettably, we must admit that today we face other challenges—ones that are far more urgent and pressing. Although the moderator said that we need to calm everyone down, those pressing problems haven't gone anywhere; they are still right here.  The alarming trends we are witnessing on the international stage force us to think not so much about how to organize global interaction in the coming period in a wiser, more effective, and more equitable manner—although all of this certainly is very vital —but rather, first and foremost, about how to preserve global peace and security right now, under conditions where many former legal norms have been discarded, while new ones have yet to emerge.🔥🔥🔥  What must be done to avoid the most catastrophic scenarios? Responsibility for our common future is by no means an abstract slogan. It is a set of practical actions aimed at preventing humanity from sliding to the brink of survival and avoiding the irreversible.  The world has arrived at a decisive, pivotal turning point in its development. And this is by no means just about politics—politics, as always, is merely a derivative of profound changes. Changes are taking place across all fields: from practically every technology to the social structure of societies, from climate to medicine, from warfare to bioethics, from the future of energy to demographic shifts, from widespread digitalization and artificial intelligence to entirely new models of economic development—and the list could go on and on. Collectively, this creates the conditions for a qualitative transformation  ["Качественной трансформации"]. We cannot yet assess all of its circumstances and their consequences unequivocally or in full, if only for the simple reason that the aforementioned changes are unfolding simultaneously, and their impact on societies and states is fraught with contradictions.🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 But I will return to this point later.  The scale of the changes—both those that have already occurred and those yet to come—is simply enormous, and we seem to understand this; it is no accident that there is currently so much debate about the future, often with a pronounced tinge of anxiety due to uncertainty and unpredictability. Yet, even though humanity senses these massive shifts, it has nonetheless not yet truly fully grasped the caliber of the challenge it faces. This is the beginning of a completely new, absolutely new reality. Threats and dangers are closely intertwined with opportunities and prospects, and they are, at the same time, inseparable from one another. Our entire way of life is changing.  Let me emphasize once again: this is not just—or even so much—about a shift in the balance of power among nations or the redistribution of economic and technological influence, though all of this is, of course, important and is indeed taking place. What matters most is that the changes are affecting the biological and moral-ethical ["Морально-нравственную"] nature of human beings, their very essence, our mode of existence, and the foundations of our worldview. Technology opens up prospects that are literally fantastic for extending and improving the quality of life. Yet, at the same time, it raises to a new level the potential for total destruction—brought about, unfortunately, by military conflicts, rapid environmental degradation, or a loss of control over unleashed technological processes.🔥🔥🔥  Understandably, such an atmosphere only provokes heightened nervousness among individuals and societies, as well as a rise in internal tension stemming from uncertainty and a lack of understanding of what tomorrow will bring. One consequence is the domestic political fever gripping many countries, especially since traditional party systems are increasingly less reflective of the rapidly changing social structure.   For any state, no matter how it is organized or what cultural and historical traditions it relies upon, internal stability—I think you will agree with me—is always more important than anything else. To preserve it, governments may take a wide variety of actions, including those that influence the state of affairs abroad—in neighboring countries, regions, and indeed the world as a whole—in other words, regrettably exporting instability. All of this only exacerbates and intensifies the friction—the heat, if one may put it that way—of the international environment.  No matter which scenario plays out in the world in the coming years, the continuation of international conflicts is, regrettably, highly likely. This is also due, in part, to the fact that the ongoing fundamental shifts and the opportunities opening up here stimulate and fuel ambitions, as well as a willingness to take risks for the sake of what appears to be a major gain. One would like to be mistaken in this assessment, but unfortunately, these are precisely the persistent trends of today.  Yet, we are confident that from a strategic perspective, as the world moves away from Western hegemony, the global situation will gradually change for the better, toward a more stable, democratic, and free multipolar international order. However, it is also obvious that on the path to such a world order, risks of various kinds await us—affecting states, societies, and every single individual. In the context of fundamental shifts, this is inevitable, which is why minimizing risks at every level—from the global to the personal—is today the primary task for responsible decision-makers in politics, business, science, and life in general. Much depends on these people. Responsibility also lies in helping people realize these risks and be prepared for them, so that an individual or a family is not left alone to face challenges in the sphere of security, in a shifting labor market, in the digital space, and so forth.  What is highly important right now, in my view? Is it caution and prudence, so as not to get caught under an avalanche of uncontrolled changes? Or is it an active, assertive approach aimed at overcoming unfavorable scenarios or leveraging the circumstances for one's own purposes? There is no straightforward answer here; in each specific case, a specific course of action is appropriate.  Decision-makers are, of course, trying to adapt to what is unfolding. However, under the conditions of what is now called a polycrisis—comprehensive and pervasive—it's objectively very difficult for them to break away from the daily management grind and look beyond it.  Immediate responsibility is enormous; a mistake can carry a very high price tag, including for the future. Today's tasks often push strategic goals into the background. While this is certainly understandable, it is also highly, exceptionally dangerous. It is impossible to respond to many current challenges without taking into account how our actions today will impact our future. As a well-known classic of domestic political thought once put it, one must not fail to see the forest for the trees [Sophia:  Lenin,  "За деревьями не видят леса" 1917. Written between the July Days crisis and the October Revolution, Lenin used this text to heavily criticize the Menshevik leader Julius Martov. Lenin argued that Martov and other moderate socialists were entirely missing the "forest"—the foundational shifts in class power and the inevitable slide toward a military dictatorship or civil war—because they were obsessing over the "trees" of legalistic details, parliamentary procedures, and fragile compromises with the Provisional Government ].    So, what does the big picture look like? It is obvious that the mechanisms for aligning the interests and actions of states, created in previous periods, are no longer capable of fully and effectively performing their regulatory function. This is not because they are inherently bad, but because the conditions in which and for which they were once created have changed. The emerging new reality will, of course, foster the creation of new instruments, but this is a very long process. Let us speak frankly: some international organizations right now often do not mitigate risks, but at times generate and provoke them, serving the interests of a single country or a group of nations. Yet, that is not what they were created for.   Criticism is also directed at such a foundational structure as the United Nations, which, in accordance with its Charter, is called upon to play the role of the central coordinating mechanism in world affairs. Of course, this criticism is by no means always objective, but there are also well-founded concerns. This is partly due to the fact that the UN—although it is the most representative global organization—is in reality managed much less collegially and democratically than was originally intended. A limited group of Western countries, a clear global minority, exerts disproportionate influence, seeking to appropriate governance functions for themselves.  And since the actual influence of these states is declining in favor of an increasingly independent and confident global majority, the imbalances of the UN structure are becoming ever more pronounced. This is a systemic problem that cannot be solved overnight.  Russia has supported—both in the past and in the present—the idea of a just reform of the United Nations, but this reform is impossible without an internal consensus, which is currently difficult to achieve. I repeat: we consistently advocate for the UN structure to reflect the full diversity of the world, and for a much more substantial role in the organization to be played by the countries of Asia, Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East. At the same time, it is important to bear in mind that the transformation of the UN is by no means limited to expanding the Security Council and other measures for a more balanced geographical representation of countries in international governance bodies; it also entails a new substance and content for the organization's work, as well as its priority fields of activity, including forward-looking ones, especially since global changes are creating a great many new dilemmas that simply did not exist before.  The most obvious example is the question of artificial intelligence, with which all of us have yet to learn to live and work. How will its rapid development affect the intellectual level of humanity itself, its spiritual and cultural heritage? It is no accident that a concept such as 'mindful digitalization' is being discussed—meaning a rejection of the uncontrolled introduction of such technologies into areas that have always been important and sensitive to human moral development. Furthermore, the socio-humanitarian aspects of the proliferation of artificial intelligence are currently being analyzed even more closely and thoroughly than the technical or economic ones. Experts are increasingly speaking with alarm about the fact that the proliferation of artificial intelligence could become yet another attempt to bring everyone down to a lowest common denominator, to the erasure of individuality ["Обезличиванию" ] —this time through the use of algorithms configured by someone else. Such digital totalitarianism would be just as dead-end, bleak, and anti-human as the familiar examples of totalitarian societies of the past.  And yet another significant question—one that is already relevant today and will become even more pressing in the near future—is precisely this: how can states transitioning to an increasingly digitalized base ensure their sovereignty in this sphere? That is to say, how can they guarantee their security and distinct identity without cutting themselves off from global progress and without falling behind in technological development?  Another area in which science and technology are fundamentally changing the world is the human capacity to interfere deeply in what was previously considered the sole prerogative of the Creator: genetic modifications of organisms, influence over the formation of personality, and the programming of human behavior and even modes of thought. It is essential to unite the efforts of nations and communities to jointly seek universally acceptable solutions to these highly delicate, defining, and truly existential questions of being.  It would be logical to carry out such work within the framework of international organizations. However, many of them, as I have already noted, are subject to the excessive influence of Western countries, which are interested not in universal progress, but solely in maintaining their own power. The institutions that were effective after World War II do not reflect the reality of the second quarter of the current century. Is it possible to effectively reform them so that they correspond to contemporary realities? The question remains open.  New international communities are also emerging, brought about by the current global situation. They undoubtedly hold great promise, whether they are various regional alliances or structures that are already global in scope, as BRICS has become. However, it must be admitted that they all face a great deal of work in defining their institutional functions, the optimal areas for their application, and the limits of their own capabilities. Of course, one should not expect relatively recently emerged structures to quickly reshape the world around them or give final shape to its multipolar model; this is a long and thorny path with many unknowns, but it will, without a doubt, yield results.  Does this mean that for now, we are doomed to chaos? No, rendering such a verdict is, without a doubt, premature. Generally speaking, a world regulated by means of clearly codified norms [ "Чётко прописанных норм" ] and regulatory institutions—an ordered world, so to speak—is a recent invention of the past century. All previous centuries managed without it. Things turned out, as we know, to put it mildly, with varying degrees of success: arrogance, envy, and greed have always been present in world politics, and they are still encountered today.  Nonetheless, responsible powers have always competed in one way or another, yet they also worked together, constructing and building systems of relations among themselves and with other, smaller states, and on the whole, as a rule, they sought to maintain stability.  Today, against the backdrop of the crisis of institutions and the degradation of international law, an immense responsibility falls upon major powers—one that is commensurate with their own immense capabilities. Such states possess the potential for actions capable of instantly altering global trends toward greater predictability and security, or conversely, toward deepening, exacerbating, and triggering a collapse of all existing problems. This potential is multiplied exponentially by the already mentioned new technologies, and it is obvious that the future of the entire world, and therefore of every individual, depends on how effective risk management will be during this phase of drastic changes.  The lack of universally recognized rules, the absence of an understanding of the principle of equal and indivisible security, or the abrogation of this principle often drives selfish behavior, and in certain cases, it turns into aggressive attempts to gain unilateral advantages, exacerbate the confusion, and exploit it for one's own interests. World politics yields examples of this nearly every day. All conceivable and inconceivable taboos are being broken—I will not list them all now, as I believe those sitting in this hall understand this perfectly well. It is my deep conviction that such a complex matter as international relations still demands careful handling, compliance not only with enacted laws but also, as lawyers say, with customary law—meaning not just the letter, but also the spirit of the law, as well as established and universally recognized practice.  Moral-ethical constraints and matters of propriety are nonetheless vital, because respecting them creates the possibility for at least some form of dialogue. Conversely, the systematic failure to fulfill obligations, deception, the turning of communication into a farce and of any meaningful conversation into propaganda,  the demonstrative mockery of facts and turning them inside out for the sake of immediate gain—all of this destroys the very foundation of international coexistence.  Such a practice—if one may call it that—of conducting international affairs is both short-sighted and dangerous. A temporary advantage gained in this manner can turn into long-term failures and, most importantly, worsen the situation for everyone, since the interconnectedness of the world is not going anywhere. The principle that 'might makes right' seems at times to be the guiding rule for certain international players  who are confident in their own military-political, economic, and—as they see it—moral exceptionalism  (Sophia:  "Certain internationals playerS🤡🤡🤡?-- how many USAs are there out there ?  What is being achieved with these WIERD COVERT TERMS?  YOU THINK YOU ARE BEING VERY POLITE AND KIND? 🤡) We know perfectly well from history that this never leads to any good.  I will digress from the main topic briefly. Present here are people with very diverse viewpoints on today’s highly acute conflict—the Ukrainian conflict—and on its causes. I would like to say a few words about this. Yes, and many hundreds or even thousands of experts—your colleagues—who will be studying the materials of this current session of the Valdai Club, also have their own thoughts on this matter. I am aware, of course, that a segment of the expert community will raise a question: here is Russia talking about peace, yet it started a war. I have spoken out on this matter many times before. Nevertheless, in an assembly such as this, I will speak about it once more.  Where does the truth lie? The truth is that it was not we who wanted or started to fight; rather, they are the ones who began to fight with us.   They should not have spent years encouraging aggressive nationalism and Russophobia in Ukraine for the purpose of turning it into an instrument for fighting against Russia. NATO shouldn't have started the military exploitation of our historical territories for its own benefit, or planned its bases there. They should not have pushed the radicals in Kiev toward a coup d'état, and then pump the essentially illegal regime created in this manner with a wide variety of offensive weapons. They should not have made plans to set up concentration camps for the residents of Donbas and Crimea. They should not have crushed unarmed people with tanks, pelted them with missiles, shot them from airplanes, or burned them alive, simply because they were Russian by nationality and spirit.  There are very many more of these 'should not have' items, but I will stop there. I am certain that Russia was deliberately placed in a situation where it was simply forced—in response to this obvious aggression—to defend itself with weapons. They deliberately brought us to this point. And fundamentally, they should not have turned Russophobia, the oppression and murder of Russian people, and the destruction of Russia into state ideology, or set a goal of inflicting a strategic defeat on Russia. After all, those were their exact words, weren't they? [ "Так ведь всё и звучало, правда?" ] No one has forgotten that. We, at east, haven't forgotten.  👊🇷🇺  If we want to live—and everyone wants to live—then, as I once said in a public speech, let us live in harmony and search together for ways to make that happen. As for building trust, it is, of course, a complex and fragile process; it is very difficult to establish, and very easy to destroy.   The interests of even the closest partners cannot align completely. What, then, is there to say about countries that find themselves in relationships of rivalry, fierce competition, and—even more so—confrontation?  Sooner or later, the international situation and system will reach a state of some stable balance. Unquestionably, this is a complex, multi-faceted, and multi-layered process that requires mutual compromises, mutual accommodation, and a sober assessment of the situation—including on the part of the West. The former hegemon will inevitably have to recognize the realities of a multipolar world—this is unavoidable; just look at the development trends of the global economy—and it will need to learn to cooperate with the countries of the global majority based on respect for their core interests. This, of course, will not happen quickly. We are bound to live in an extraordinarily unstable, volatile world. The path to a new system will be replete with unexpected turns and developments—regrettably, often unpleasant and even dangerous ones.  At this point I would like to turn to our own domestic history. Russia has traversed a difficult path of profound transformations, and this process continues. Thirty-five years ago, we experienced the collapse of our state structure, which became a true tragedy for tens of millions of people who woke up overnight to find themselves living "abroad," —an event that altered their destiny and the destiny of their children. Both within our country, in Russia, and in neighboring nations, all of this led to a fundamental transformation and in world affairs as well.  I will separately note a certain naivety,  complacency ["прекраснодушие" literally means "beautiful-soulness" ] —or perhaps even carelessness—on the part of those people who headed the state during the final years of the Soviet era. Blind trust in Western partners, the belief in the possibility of some kind of "gentlemen's agreements," where it was supposedly enough to take someone at their word and agree on something—this also played a cruel joke on the Soviet Union.🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥  In retrospect, it becomes clear how destructive a role this played not only in the destiny of the USSR, but also for ensuring long-term global stability. Soviet leaders wanted to please the West, while Western leaders wanted to carve up the world to suit themselves and to get—to snatch away—their own, preferably large, share of the Soviet legacy. We can see the results. 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥  END OF PART 1  1/2   #Russia ❤️🇷🇺

DPRK THREAT-ACTOR PLAYBOOK  North Korea runs its cyber operations like a state budget line. Patient, persistent, and above all, financially motivated in ways that distinguish it from almost every other state actor.  The archive holds 130 documented incidents spanning September 1996 to September 2026. Thirty years of continuous operation. The program did not emerge fully formed; it grew alongside the regime's nuclear ambitions, and the two are now structurally linked. Sanctions constrain hard currency. Cyber operations generate it.  ---  METHODS AND VOLUME  Cyber Espionage: 65 incidents Advanced Persistent Threat Operations: 60 incidents Critical Infrastructure Mapping: 26 incidents Infrastructure Attacks: 24 incidents Malware Distribution: 18 incidents Ransomware Campaigns: 17 incidents Cryptocurrency Theft: 17 incidents Supply Chain Exploitation: 16 incidents  The top two categories overlap considerably by design. DPRK APT operations are the delivery mechanism; espionage is frequently the payload. What separates North Korea from most state actors is what sits below that: cryptocurrency theft and ransomware running in parallel with traditional espionage. Pyongyang does not draw a clean line between intelligence collection and revenue generation. Sometimes the same access serves both purposes.  Critical infrastructure mapping at 26 incidents deserves attention. That number does not represent 26 attacks. It represents 26 instances of documented reconnaissance. The attacks, if they come, come later.  ---  HOW THEY WORK  The operational signature is patience and cover. North Korean operators routinely maintain access inside target networks for months before doing anything visible. When they do move, it is often to exfiltrate, occasionally to steal funds, and in a smaller number of cases to stage for potential disruptive action.  The social engineering tradecraft is unusually developed. Operation Dream Job, documented as recently as August 2026, has been running in recognizable form for years. The premise is simple: contact a defense or technology sector employee, pose as a recruiter, build rapport, deliver a malicious file or link embedded in what looks like a job application process. The August 2026 iteration added CVE-2026-68820, a Windows kernel privilege escalation zero-day, to the lure chain. Same concept, meaningfully upgraded technical execution.  That combination, a well-worn social engineering framework married to fresh exploit development, is characteristic. DPRK operators are not purely tool-reusers and they are not purely capability developers. They blend.  Supply chain exploitation appears in 16 documented incidents. That number has been climbing. The logic is straightforward: compromise a vendor with broad customer access once, and the downstream reach multiplies the effort. North Korean operators have applied this across software distribution channels, managed service providers, and development toolchains.  ---  THE FINANCIAL DIMENSION  This is where North Korea differs structurally from China, Russia, or Iran.  Seventeen documented cryptocurrency theft incidents. Seventeen documented ransomware campaigns. These are not side projects. UN Panel of Experts assessments have repeatedly found that DPRK cyber operations fund prohibited weapons programs directly. The Lazarus Group and affiliated clusters have been attributed to cryptocurrency platform compromises totaling billions of dollars across multiple years. The September 2026 Security Affairs Round 597 digest captured continued activity in this space alongside document exfiltration operations, which is a good illustration of how the programs run concurrently rather than sequentially.  Ransomware as espionage cover is a documented pattern. Deploy ransomware, collect payment, but the primary objective was data access. The ransom demand provides both revenue and a convenient explanation for the intrusion that does not require the victim to acknowledge what was actually taken.  ---  INSTITUTIONAL ARCHITECTURE  North Korea's cyber operations sit under Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB), which also controls foreign intelligence and special operations. The organizational consolidation matters because it means cyber, signals, and human intelligence operations can be coordinated at the command level rather than deconflicted after the fact.  Lazarus Group is the most publicly attributed cluster, but the attribution landscape is segmented. Bluenoroff handles financial operations. Andariel has been associated with critical infrastructure targeting and ransomware. APT38 (overlapping with Bluenoroff in many frameworks) focuses on financial system intrusions. In practice the clusters share infrastructure and personnel, and the boundaries in public reporting reflect analytic conventions more than hard operational divisions.  ---  RECENT INDICATORS  The September 2026 DPRK Foreign Ministry statement is worth treating as a data point, not just diplomatic noise. Pyongyang issues sovereignty doctrine statements in coordinated patterns. They function as preemptive rhetorical cover for activities the regime knows will attract scrutiny, and they are systematically amplified through Russian and Chinese state media. The September 2026 statement coincided with documented DPRK weapons and personnel provision to Russia for Ukraine operations, an alignment that has material implications for technology transfer and operational coordination between the programs.  The Tenable-SentinelOne joint analysis from August 2026, covering 93 CVE-actor pairs, found state APTs and criminal actors converging on identical edge infrastructure vulnerabilities. North Korean operators appear in that dataset. The convergence is a deliberate feature in some cases. When your intrusion looks indistinguishable from a criminal ransomware operator's intrusion, attribution slows and the intelligence or financial objective proceeds.  The FBI's September 2026 global threat framework names North Korea alongside China, Russia, and Iran in multi-domain operations against U.S. interests. North Korea does not lead that assessment in terms of overall threat volume. China holds that position. But the FBI framework documents DPRK operations spanning espionage, economic theft, and what the framework terms transnational repression, meaning operations against North Korean diaspora communities and defectors abroad. That last category is underreported relative to its actual frequency.  ---  WHAT TO WATCH  Three things.  First, the Dream Job template keeps evolving. It has absorbed zero-days before and it will again. Any organization in defense, aerospace, technology, or cryptocurrency that is not actively training employees on this specific social engineering vector has a gap.  Second, the Russia alignment is not cosmetic. DPRK provision of artillery, missiles, and reportedly personnel to Russia creates conditions for reciprocal technology transfer. If Russian cyber tooling or infrastructure begins appearing in DPRK operations at higher frequency, that alignment has moved beyond weapons logistics.  Third, cryptocurrency infrastructure remains a primary target. North Korean operators have demonstrated the ability to compromise exchange platforms, DeFi protocols, and individual custody solutions. The sophistication of these operations has increased year over year. The seventeen incidents in the archive represent confirmed attributions. The actual number is higher.  Thirty years in, the program is larger, better resourced, and more technically capable than it was at any prior point. The financial motive is structural, not opportunistic. It does not go away when diplomatic conditions shift, because the weapons programs the revenue funds do not pause for diplomacy either.  foreigninterference.org #foreigninterference #CyberEspionage #AdvancedPersistentThreatOperations #CriticalInfrastructureMapping #InfrastructureAttacks

🚨TIMELINES, PATTERNS, THE ILLEGAL ILLICIT NETWORK & ANOTHER "UNPRECEDENTED" EVENT  👉Ninety-One Billion Dollars  On October 1, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury designated the A7 Network as a significant transnational criminal organization.  The A7 Network processed more than 2,000 transactions per day. Its total transaction volume exceeded 7.5 trillion rubles $91.5 billion. That represents approximately 13% of Russia's entire foreign trade in 2025. One network. Thirteen percent of a G20 economy's international commerce.  Treasury deployed three instruments simultaneously.  FinCEN issued a proposed rule prohibiting any transmittal of funds involving A7 Sub-Agents. That's the plumbing-level ban every bank in the world is now on notice that processing a payment through an A7 entity is a potential violation.  FinCEN issued an Alert with red flags to help financial institutions identify A7 activity. That's the map handed to the private sector the same FinCEN Exchange mechanism that briefed banks on Operation Economic Outcast two weeks ago.  OFAC designated the entire A7 Network as a transnational criminal organization. That's the nuclear option every asset, every entity, every Sub-Agent, every transaction blocked.  Three tools. One target. One press release. One morning.  Here's what the A7 Network actually is.  A constellation of purpose-built shell companies called "Sub-Agents" spread across third-country jurisdictions. Each Sub-Agent is designed to receive and send payments that make sanctioned transactions look like ordinary commerce. Falsified trade documents. Falsified import-export records. Misleading goods descriptions. The entire architecture exists to make illegal payments invisible inside the legitimate financial system.  The Sub-Agents' websites and bank accounts are controlled by A7 Network staff using custom-built VPNs that mask their true location. The companies are shells. The websites are facades. The bank accounts are funnels. The VPNs hide who's actually pressing the buttons.  This isn't a few bad actors using the financial system. This is a parallel financial system, purpose-built to evade the one that every government in the world has spent two decades making transparent.  Now read who used it.  Russia 13% of its foreign trade flowed through A7's infrastructure.  Iran  the Central Bank of Iran and the IRGC used A7 Sub-Agents to move funds through the international financial system.  Hamas  A7 facilitated transactions for Iran-backed terrorist organizations, including Hamas.  North Korea  A7 Sub-Agents facilitated transactions related to North Korean hacks of cryptocurrency exchanges.  Ransomware operators cybercriminals used A7 to move funds.  Iran's shadow fleet  one A7 Sub-Agent directly transacted with tankers, shipping companies, and front companies used to transport and sell Iranian oil in violation of sanctions. That same Sub-Agent received nearly $140 million from Iranian sanctions evaders.  Iranian weapons procurement a separate Sub-Agent transferred $1.6 million to a company linked to Iranian weapons procurement.  Every adversary this series has documented. Russia. Iran. IRGC. Hamas. North Korea. Ransomware. All of them. Through the same pipes. At the same time.  The network even built its own cryptocurrency.  The A7A5 token a ruble-backed digital token issued by Old Vector LLC, which OFAC designated in August 2025. Created specifically for A7 members to evade sanctions and transact internationally. A purpose-built sanctions evasion cryptocurrency.  Three weeks ago, this series documented a cartel mining farm in the mountains of Puebla 300 GPUs making coins from stolen electricity because the existing crypto rails were being monitored. The A7 Network did the same thing at the institutional level it built its own token because existing tokens were being screened.  When the transparent rail gets too transparent, the adversary builds a parallel rail. When the parallel rail gets designated, the adversary builds a token for the parallel rail. Each layer of evasion produces a new layer of enforcement. Each layer of enforcement produces a new layer of evasion.  $17 billion processed between January 2025 and June 2026. Eighteen months.  $91.5 billion in total transaction volume. Thirteen percent of Russia's foreign trade.  $140 million received from Iranian sanctions evaders by a single Sub-Agent.  2,000 transactions per day.  Those numbers existed inside the global financial system. They moved through banks. They cleared through payment networks. They appeared on ledgers as ordinary commercial activity. And the entire time, the money was flowing from Russia to Iran to Hamas to North Korea to ransomware operators through a network of shell companies controlled by a convicted criminal fraudster named Ilan Shor, operating from behind custom VPNs across multiple jurisdictions.  The transparent rail caught it. FinCEN mapped it. OFAC designated it. The Alert went out to every financial institution in the world. The proposed rule will prohibit any bank from processing A7 payments. The UK's National Crime Agency flagged $86 billion in A7-linked flows in August. And today Treasury tore the whole thing up by the roots.  Yesterday, the last American soldier left Iraq. Today, Treasury designated a $91.5 billion shadow banking network that served every adversary on earth.  The rifle went home. The pen went to work. And the pen found $91.5 billion moving through purpose-built shell companies, falsified trade documents, and a custom cryptocurrency serving Russia, Iran, Hamas, North Korea, and ransomware operators through the same pipes, at the same time, disguised as ordinary commerce.  Follow the pen.  The source is the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Press Release sb0644, October 1, 2026.  I am the guy on the couch, and you have been debriefed.

“온체인에 올리기만 하면 팔린다?…RWA도 이용자부터 알아야”  [STO써밋 2026] 크리스 인 플룸네트워크 대표 거래소·네오뱅크·디파이 연계 유통 전략 제시 “기존 상품 그대로 옮겨선 투자자 끌어오기 어려워” "한국 금융상품·문화자산, 해외 투자자 접근성 높여야"  실물연계자산(RWA) 시장에서 성과를 내려면 기존 금융상품을 블록체인으로 옮기는 데 그치지 않고 이용자의 수요와 투자 방식에 맞춰 상품과 유통 경로를 바꿔야 한다는 제언이 나왔다.  투자자가 이미 이용하는 거래소와 금융서비스에서 토큰화 자산에 접근할 수 있어야 실제 자금 유입으로 이어진다는 설명이다.  크리스 인 플룸네트워크 공동창업자 겸 대표는 1일 서울 여의도 한국거래소(KRX) 컨퍼런스홀에서 열린 '이데일리 STO 써밋 2026'에서 '차세대 RWA: 실물자산의 온체인화'를 주제로 발표하며 이같이 밝혔다.  인 대표는 "대부분은 기존 상품을 그대로 온체인에 올려놓고 잘 작동하기를 바라지만 실제로는 그렇지 않다"며 "유통과 이용자를 먼저 고려해야 온체인에서 실질적인 가치를 만들어낼 수 있다"고 말했다.   온체인은 자산의 발행과 거래 등을 블록체인상에서 처리하는 방식을 뜻한다.  인 대표는 맥도날드의 해외 진출을 예로 들었다. 같은 햄버거를 팔더라도 국가별로 메뉴와 매장 경험을 달리하듯 금융상품도 새로운 시장의 이용자가 무엇을 원하고 어떤 방식으로 상품을 이용하는지 파악해야 한다는 설명이다.  그는 자산을 온체인에 발행하고 대대적으로 홍보해도 실제 투자자금이 들어오지 않는 사례가 많다고 지적했다.   상품을 먼저 내놓고 수요가 생기기를 기다리기보다 이용자와 유통 경로를 파악한 뒤 이에 맞춰 상품을 설계해야 한다고 강조했다.  RWA 시장의 성장 여건으로는 스테이블코인 시장 확대와 규제 변화, 국제 정세 불안에 따른 자금 이동을 꼽았다.   인 대표는 "온체인 스테이블코인 규모는 3000억 달러(약 407조원)를 넘어섰고 이제는 관심을 가질 만큼 충분히 큰 시장이 됐다"며 "국제 정세 불안으로 자금과 사업 거점을 옮기려는 움직임도 나타나고 있다"고 말했다.  국경과 거래 시간의 제약을 줄일 수 있다는 점도 토큰화의 이점으로 꼽았다.   투자자가 여러 국가와 자산군에 자금을 배분하기 쉬워지고 금융회사도 해외 고객을 확보할 기회가 커진다는 설명이다.  인 대표는 "24시간 운영되는 국제 시장에서는 전 세계에서 자금과 자산을 훨씬 빠르게 옮길 수 있다"며 "기업들도 전 세계를 대상으로 경쟁하고 사업을 펼칠 수 있다”고 말했다.  이어 "기존에는 세계적인 대형 자산운용사를 따라잡아야 했다"며 "온체인에 새로운 시장이 만들어진다면 신생 기업도 그 기회를 활용해 이용자를 확보할 수 있다"고 덧붙였다.  실제 투자 수요를 확보할 유통 경로로는 중앙화 거래소와 네오뱅크(인터넷 은행), 탈중앙화금융(DeFi, 디파이) 프로토콜을 제시했다. 중앙화 거래소에는 스테이블코인 자금이 모여 있고, 네오뱅크는 이를 일상 결제에 쓰려는 수요를 바탕으로 성장하고 있다고 설명했다.  인 대표는 "규모를 키우려면 가장 중요한 것은 자금이 어디에 얼마나 있는지 파악하는 일"이라며 "스테이블코인을 쓰기 위해 네오뱅크로 자금을 옮기는 사람이 많아지면서 이 분야가 빠르게 성장하고 있다"고 말했다.  디파이 대출 시장에 대해서는 상대적으로 자금 규모가 작지만 새로운 금융서비스를 실험하는 곳으로 평가했다. 이곳에서 시작한 서비스가 거래소와 네오뱅크로 확산할 수 있다는 설명이다.  인 대표는 "온체인 대출 시장은 자금 규모가 아주 크지는 않지만 많은 실험이 시작되는 곳"이라며 "원하는 시장과 이용자에게 도달하려면 세 영역에 모두 진출해야 한다"고 강조했다.  투자자의 신뢰도 주요 과제로 꼽았다. 인 대표는 "해킹 사고가 이어지면서 이용자들은 안전하다고 느끼는 몇몇 서비스로 모이려 한다"며 "이용자들이 모인 곳에서 상품을 제공하는 것이 가장 중요하다"고 말했다.  한국 금융회사의 해외 진출 가능성도 강조했다. 기존에는 해외에 금융상품을 공급하려면 현지 법인을 설립하거나 별도 상장 절차를 밟아야 해 시간과 비용이 많이 들었다는 설명이다.  인 대표는 "온체인에서는 기존 국내 시장에 금융상품을 공급하면서 미국과 중남미, 유럽 등으로 시장을 넓힐 수 있다"며 "한국 기업도 한 시장에서만 상품을 파는 대신 여러 시장에 진출해 매출을 늘리고 글로벌 브랜드로 성장할 기회가 있다"고 말했다.  한국 자산에 대한 해외 투자자의 접근성을 높여야 한다는 점도 짚었다. 한국은 개인투자자와 금융산업 기반이 탄탄하고 금융상품뿐 아니라 문화·미디어 분야에서도 해외 수요가 높다고 평가했다.  인 대표는 "한국의 문화와 미디어는 이미 세계적으로 인기가 높다"며 "이런 자산을 금융상품으로 만들고 해외 투자자가 접근할 수 있도록 하면 해외로 나가는 자금 대신 국내로 들어오는 자금을 크게 늘릴 수 있다"고 말했다.  🗞n.news.naver.com/article/018…

JUNE 24th, 2026  Election Crime Bureau Releases Landmark Evidence Dossier: “The 2020 Election – An Attack Upon  U.S. Critical Infrastructure”  The Election Crime Bureau today released a comprehensive, fully cited investigative report, “The 2020  Election – An Attack Upon U.S. Critical Infrastructure,” documenting ten coordinated attack vectors  against America’s election infrastructure in the 2020 general election. The report compiles more than 824  distinct findings supported by over 2,517 citations drawn from court records, government documents,  sworn testimony, and technical forensics. Full documentation is available at  ElectionCrimeBureau.com/Evid….   “People have been told for years there is ‘no evidence,’” said Patrick Colbeck with Mike Lindell’s Election  Crime Bureau. “This report does not ask you to trust us. It asks you to read the evidence, check the  citations, and decide for yourself.”   A national‑security framing, not just politics  The report treats U.S. elections as what federal law already says they are: designated critical  infrastructure on par with the power grid and financial systems. It concludes that in the jurisdictions that  decided the 2020 presidential outcome, the evidentiary backbone of the election—ballot images, logs,  tapes, surveillance video, and voter‑history records—was so badly compromised that key outcomes are  now “functionally unauditable and therefore unreliable as a matter of national security.”   “As this record shows, you cannot call an election ‘secure’ if you cannot reconstruct what the machines  did, who changed which ballots, or where hundreds of thousands of ballots came from,” the report states.   Readers can download the full report and its detailed appendices at  ElectionCrimeBureau.com/Evid…, where each finding is organized, classified, and backed by  primary‑source references.   Ten distinct attack vectors  The report identifies ten interlocking attack vectors through which the 2020 election infrastructure has  been manipulated, shielded from scrutiny, or both.  1. Election Record Integrity (Attack Vector 01)  The report catalogs dozens of instances where voter rolls, ballot images, adjudication logs, memory cards,  tally tapes, drop‑box videos, and voter‑history records were missing, destroyed, wiped, or never produced  in key jurisdictions. It highlights that federal law requires preservation of federal election records for 22  months and documents large‑scale non‑compliance.   "Michigan counted 499,850 more ballots than voters. Pennsylvania counted 155,053 more. In Fulton  County alone, 22,534 more ballots were counted than voters recorded. Each discrepancy independently  exceeds its state's margin of victory."  2. Electronic Voting System Integrity (Attack Vector 02)  The report shows that voting systems in multiple states were operated outside their certified  configurations, including uncertified software updates, extreme error rates, weak or shared passwords,  plaintext encryption keys stored next to votes, and auto‑overwriting logs.  "319 classified-severity vulnerabilities. Suppressed for 22 months. Those machines are still certified.  They will be used in 2026. The question is not whether they were vulnerable in 2020. The question is  whether they are vulnerable today."  3. Election Results Certification Integrity (Attack Vector 03)  The report details irregularities in certification, including certifications under duress, over unresolved  discrepancies, and in some cases contrary to statutory requirements and canvassers’ written objections.  "Certification was not a checkpoint — it was a closing mechanism. In every decisive battleground state,  officials certified results over missing records, statutory violations, mathematical impossibilities, and  canvassers operating under duress. The last institutional brake on a defective election was never  applied; it was bypassed, coerced, or falsified out of the way."  4. Judicial Malfeasance (Attack Vector 04)  The report dissects the “64 cases lost” narrative, separating procedural dismissals, voluntary withdrawals  under sanction threats, and a small number of cases that reached limited discovery.  "They didn't need to rig the count. They needed the pre-election challenge to be too early, the post election challenge to be too late, the discovery request to be denied, the forensic sample to be too  small, the protocol order to never arrive, and the attorney who kept filing to lose her license. By the  time the public was told the courts found no evidence, the courts had made certain they never would."  5. Information Control (Attack Vector 05)  The document outlines how officials, agencies, and platforms coordinated a unified “most secure election  in history” narrative even as internal risk reports (e.g., CISA’s TLP‑AMBER summaries) showed hundreds  of critical vulnerabilities and active exploitation.  "A federally certified critical-infrastructure system is resilient only if its public so that its courts and its  Congress can see and debate its actual performance. When the government classifies the vulnerability  data, suppresses the opposition research, censors the witnesses, and designates the questioners as  terrorism threats — it has not secured the election. It has secured the narrative."  6. Financial Influence (Attack Vector 06)  The report describes how targeted private funding streams skewed resources toward select counties and  operations, creating asymmetric leverage over how elections were run in key metros.  "Treasury OFAC has designated Cartel de los Soles as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist organization.  If any dollar attributable to a designated foreign terrorist organization reached U.S. election infrastructure  through the unverified online donation channels documented in this report, the legal exposure is not a  campaign finance violation. It is material support for terrorism — up to life imprisonment."  7. As AI systems become more capable at cybersecurity, an important question is emerging around who should be allowed to use that capability and under what conditions. Much of the current safety debate focuses on controlling access through proprietary models, API policies, usage restrictions, and safeguards designed to prevent advanced cyber capabilities from being misused.  The problem is that cybersecurity is adversarial.  Attackers do not respect acceptable-use policies, enterprise procurement rules, data residency requirements, or third-party risk controls. They can run open models locally, modify them, remove safeguards, and build systems around capabilities that already exist. Defenders are the ones operating under the strictest constraints, and that creates an asymmetric form of safety where legitimate security teams are restricted from capabilities that determined attackers can still obtain.  Cybersecurity has been through a version of this debate before, in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Vulnerability disclosure, exploit development, scanners, and offensive security tools were all controversial, because the same technology could be used to attack systems or defend them. Over time, tools like Nmap and Metasploit, public vulnerability research, and reproducible exploits became part of the basic infrastructure of modern security. The takeaway was not that dual-use technology is harmless, but that restricting the knowledge available to defenders does not make the underlying offensive capability disappear.  AI brings that argument back at a much larger scale.  The question is not whether these capabilities can be misused. They can. The question is whether restricting legitimate access meaningfully restricts attackers once capable open models already exist. We think it increasingly restricts defenders instead. Machine-speed attacks require machine-speed defense, and defenders need models they can run, control, and improve inside the systems they are responsible for protecting.

A Dutch Cybersecurity Nonprofit Was Breached by an AI Agent That Described Its Own Attack as “Loud and Very, Very Messy.”  The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, a volunteer organization that scans the internet for vulnerable systems and notifies their owners suffered an intrusion that it described as the first agentic-AI-powered attack it had ever seen.  The agent exploited a technical vulnerability (not Citrix NetScaler, DIVD clarified), then autonomously performed post-exploitation activities: deciding its next step after every action, at the speed of light, with what DIVD called “sloppy logic or pattern.”  The agent even interfered with its own adversary-in-the-middle attack via password spraying a self inflicted operational error that gave investigators a detailed trail to reconstruct. DIVD reported the incident to the police, the Dutch data protection authority, and the National Cyber Security Centre.  The organization said the attack was serious, but the agent’s “loud” behavior left sufficient evidence for reverse engineering.  The question no one has answered yet: was this a targeted attack, an experiment, or an autonomous agent that simply wandered in?  #AgenticAI #DIVD #IncidentResponse

The attackers exploited TWO previously unknown vulnerabilities in the Zammad helpdesk platform:  * CVE-2026-102489 — remote code execution as the Zammad user * CVE-2026-102490 — local privilege escalation from Zammad user to ROOT  The vulnerabilities were exploited against DIVD on September 21 — nine days before their public disclosure.  But this incident has another unusual element.  DIVD says the attack's modus operandi indicates an AGENTIC AI-POWERED ATTACK.  After compromising the environment, the autonomous agent reportedly selected its next actions based on previous results rather than simply executing a predetermined sequence.  DIVD described the activity as:  "loud and very very messy."  The agent moved quickly but made operational mistakes and left extensive forensic evidence behind.  One example was particularly unusual:  The agent reportedly interfered with its OWN adversary-in-the-middle operation while simultaneously performing password spraying.  It also left comments explaining many of its actions — effectively giving investigators additional evidence about how it was making decisions.  Now we know the initial technical path.  CVE-2026-102489 Zammad 6.3.0 → 6.5.4  Session hijacking can lead to remote code execution as the Zammad user.  CVE-2026-102490  The local Zammad user can escalate privileges to ROOT.  The Dutch NCSC confirms BOTH vulnerabilities are being actively exploited.  ⚠️ More importantly:  CVE-2026-102490 IS STILL NOT FIXED.  DIVD is now scanning the internet and notifying owners of vulnerable Zammad installations.  Its recommendation:  * Upgrade to Zammad 7 * Or TAKE THE SYSTEM OFFLINE  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This incident deserves attention beyond the two zero-days.  It provides a rare real-world look at what autonomous offensive agents may look like today:  FAST. AUTONOMOUS. IMPERFECT. NOISY.  But still capable of successfully compromising a real cybersecurity organization.  The important question is what happens when these agents stop making obvious mistakes.  csirt.divd.nl/cases/DIVD-202… #Zammad #ZeroDay #AgenticAI #AISecurity #CyberAttack #ThreatIntel #CyberSecurity #DDW

🦠🧬 Could a microbial exposure in early life leave a “pre-cancerous memory” in the colon decades before cancer emerges?  A new 2026 bioRxiv study proposes a provocative model:  EARLY-LIFE MICROBIOME → epithelial stem-cell remodeling → persistent bacterial niche → increased susceptibility to colorectal cancer At the center is: enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF)  and its metalloprotease toxin:  BFT — B. fragilis toxin.  Using a vertical-transmission mouse model, Russell et al. show that neonatal ETBF exposure remodels the developing colonic epithelium, expands stem/progenitor programs, promotes precancerous lesions in genetically susceptible mice, and establishes intracellular bacterial reservoirs inside those lesions.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  The emerging pathway is:  EARLY-LIFE ETBF  ↓ lamina propria niche entry ↓ Fragipain (Fpn) → BFT activation ↓  LGR5⁺ STEM CELLS ↑ WNT ↑ ATOH1⁺ SECRETORY PROGENITORS ↑ ↓ crypt remodeling ↓ PRECANCEROUS ACF ↓ intracellular ETBF communities ↓ potential persistent oncogenic niche But remarkably, early colonization with non-toxigenic B. fragilis (NTBF) can interrupt this sequence.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full 👶 Timing is EVERYTHING ETBF is not simply another CRC-associated bacterium. During a restricted neonatal developmental window, ETBF can penetrate the mucus and access the: LAMINA PROPRIA through goblet-cell-associated antigen passages. That places BFT close to colonic crypt stem cells.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full The authors therefore asked whether exposure during this unusually permissive developmental state could permanently alter epithelial biology. Their vertical-transmission model is particularly interesting because pups acquire ETBF naturally from colonized dams rather than through direct neonatal antibiotic manipulation.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full 🔬 BFT directly remodels epithelial cells In primary colonic organoids, only 3 hours of active BFT exposure caused:  epithelial-junction disruption  F-actin disorganization  dense cellular structures  Ki67 proliferation ↑.  Inactive BFT did not reproduce these changes.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  The images in Extended Data Fig. 2, page 39 make this especially clear: active BFT rapidly converts relatively organized organoids into structurally disrupted, Ki67-rich epithelial structures.  So BFT alone is sufficient to induce rapid epithelial remodeling without requiring the complete inflammatory microenvironment.  🌱 But what happens to the STEM-CELL compartment?  This is where the study becomes particularly interesting.  Neonatal ETBF exposure increased:  LGR5⁺ intestinal stem cells  along the crypt axis.  It simultaneously increased:  WNT activity and expanded: ATOH1⁺ secretory progenitors. All three effects were attenuated when either BFT or its activating protease Fpn was disrupted.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  Importantly, the fraction of Lgr5⁺ cells did not increase—the entire crypt expanded.  So ETBF appears to expand the stem-cell compartment as part of a broader proliferative remodeling program rather than merely converting cells into Lgr5⁺ identity.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  🎯 Then they ask the critical question:  Does this developmental remodeling actually increase tumor initiation?  Using:  ApcMin/+ mice  the authors examined aberrant crypt foci (ACF)—early precancerous lesions.  At only:  4 WEEKS OF AGE  neonatally ETBF-colonized animals developed substantially more ACF than mice colonized with:  Δfpn ETBF  Δbft ETBF  or uncolonized controls.  2026.09.28.755180v1.full  Figure 3 on page 32 is particularly striking: the ETBF-WT distal colon contains numerous primal, intermediate, and advanced lesions, whereas disrupting either Fpn or BFT markedly reduces the burden.  Genetic complementation restored the phenotype, strengthening the causal connection to these bacterial factors.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  ⏳ The lesions are initiated EARLY—but then PROGRESS  An important longitudinal observation:  total ACF number  was similar between weeks 4 and 8.  But their composition changed.  By 8 weeks:  smaller primal lesions tended to decrease  while  macroadenomas ≥1 mm increased significantly.  2026.09.28.755180v1.full So ETBF appears to establish lesions during an early developmental window, after which existing lesions continue progressing. This is conceptually different from continuous initiation throughout life:  EARLY HIT → LATER PROGRESSION.  📍 Why the DISTAL colon?  Interestingly, ETBF tissue colonization was comparable across:  cecum  proximal colon  distal colon.  Yet tumor initiation preferentially occurred in the: DISTAL COLON.  2026.09.28.755180v1.full  The explanation appears to involve:  WNT SIGNALING. In cecum and proximal colon, ETBF-induced Wnt activity remained largely restricted to the crypt base. But in distal colon:  WNT ACTIVITY EXTENDED UP THE CRYPT AXIS  and into underlying stromal cells.  The proliferative Ki67⁺ compartment expanded in parallel.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  The microscopy in Extended Data Fig. 8, page 49 beautifully illustrates this spatial difference.  So:  BACTERIAL EXPOSURE  is only one component.  The outcome depends on: MICROBE × DEVELOPMENTAL TIME × TISSUE LOCATION. 🔥 WNT activation occurs at the EARLIEST detectable lesion stage  In neonatal ETBF-exposed ApcMin/+ mice, even:  PRIMAL ACF  already displayed strong Wnt activation.  As lesions advanced:  WNT⁺ / Ki67⁺ spatial overlap increased.  2026.09.28.755180v1.full  Figure 4 on page 34 shows this progression particularly well.  But when ETBF colonization was delayed until:  P28  Wnt-positive ACF were not observed.  That is a crucial experiment because the bacterium is similar—the developmental context is not.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  🤯 Then comes perhaps the most surprising finding:  ETBF moves INSIDE the precancerous lesion At 8 weeks, confocal imaging revealed discrete:  INTRACELLULAR BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES — IBCs  inside ACF lesions.  Orthogonal z-stack reconstruction confirmed bacterial aggregates within the epithelial compartment.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  The images in Figure 5, page 36 are remarkable: ETBF appears as green intracellular aggregates embedded within the transformed epithelial lesion.  And this again depended strongly on:  BFT  Fpn  developmental timing.  Juvenile P28 colonization produced dramatically fewer IBCs.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  So ETBF may undergo a fascinating ecological transition:  EARLY-LIFE COLONIZER  ↓ lamina propria niche ↓ epithelial remodeling ↓ preneoplastic lesion ↓  TUMOR-ASSOCIATED INTRACELLULAR RESERVOIR  The microbe may therefore help create a niche that subsequently becomes a niche for the microbe itself.  🔄 A potential positive-feedback loop  The data suggest a provocative model:  ETBF  ↓ BFT ↓ epithelial remodeling ↓ Wnt/proliferation ↓ precancerous lesion ↓  ETBF IBC FORMATION  ↓ persistent local microbial reservoir ↓ potential continued epithelial remodeling  However, the final arrow remains hypothetical.  The authors explicitly state that whether tumor-associated IBCs remain functionally active and contribute directly to tumor progression is not yet established.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  That is an important next experiment.  🛡️ But the most translationally interesting experiment may involve a “GOOD” B. fragilis  The investigators then introduced: NON-TOXIGENIC B. FRAGILIS — NTBF before ETBF could fully establish its pathogenic tissue niche.  Timing again mattered dramatically.  NTBF at P12  → ACF ↓↓↓ NTBF at P21 → little protection. 2026.09.28.755180v1.full And the protective effect required: TYPE VI SECRETION SYSTEM — T6SS. A ΔtssC NTBF mutant failed to protect. Why? T6SS enables direct bacterial competition.  Conceptually:  NTBF  ↓ T6SS  ETBF EXCLUDED FROM TISSUE NICHE  ↓ BFT exposure ↓ ↓ Wnt/stem-cell remodeling ↓ ↓ ACF INITIATION ↓ 🧫 This is microbial ECOLOGY as cancer prevention Figure 6 on page 37 provides a compelling visual. Early P12 NTBF treatment produced substantially fewer ACF and: NO DETECTABLE IBCs whereas P21 treatment allowed both more lesions and intracellular ETBF communities. The ΔtssC strain also lost protection.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full So the therapeutic principle is not necessarily: kill the pathogenic bacterium. Instead: OCCUPY THE DEVELOPMENTAL NICHE FIRST. A commensal relative can use bacterial competition to prevent the pathobiont from accessing the compartment where it becomes carcinogenic. 🧠 This changes the conceptual timeline of MICROBE-DRIVEN CANCER The conventional model is often:  ADULT MICROBIOME DYSBIOSIS  ↓ chronic inflammation ↓ DNA damage / tumor promotion ↓  CRC  This study suggests another possibility:  NEONATAL MICROBIOME  ↓ developmental tissue access ↓  STEM-CELL STATE REPROGRAMMING  ↓ latent susceptibility ↓  PRECANCEROUS FIELD  ↓ later progression. The authors describe this as a developmental window in which microbial exposure can establish a durable epithelial vulnerability.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  🧬 And there is an intriguing connection to EARLY-ONSET CRC The authors note that early-onset CRC has risen particularly in the descending/left colon and rectum, paralleling the distal-colon susceptibility observed in their mouse model.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  They also connect their findings to recent human CRC genomic studies showing that mutational signatures from microbial genotoxins such as colibactin can be imprinted early during tumor evolution.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  But this distinction is crucial:  THIS STUDY DOES NOT SHOW THAT NEONATAL ETBF CAUSES HUMAN EARLY-ONSET CRC.  It provides a mechanistic mouse model demonstrating that developmental timing can profoundly change the carcinogenic consequences of microbial colonization.  ⚠️ Important limitations  This is currently a:  bioRxiv PREPRINT — NOT PEER REVIEWED.  The strongest tumor-initiation experiments also use: ApcMin/+ genetically predisposed mice. Therefore, whether early ETBF exposure initiates comparable disease in genetically normal hosts remains unresolved.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full The authors also acknowledge that neonatal versus juvenile experiments do not completely separate: intrinsic developmental susceptibility of epithelial cells from developmental access of ETBF to the lamina propria. Those mechanisms will require experiments that independently manipulate epithelial age and microbial tissue localization.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full And the proposed Wnt mechanism remains associative: functional perturbation is still needed to prove that Wnt activation is required for ETBF-driven lesion initiation.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full  💡 The deeper biological principle  Perhaps the most interesting lesson is that:  MICROBIAL IDENTITY ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH.  The same organism can have profoundly different consequences depending on:  WHO COLONIZES  ×  WHEN  ×  WHERE  ×  WHICH HOST GENOTYPE  ETBF arriving during a permissive developmental window:  → enters tissue → activates BFT locally → remodels stem/progenitor states → amplifies Wnt → promotes precancerous lesions → persists within those lesions.  But establish NTBF early enough:  → microbial competition → ETBF tissue exclusion → tumor initiation suppressed.  So perhaps cancer prevention can begin much earlier than we normally imagine—not by treating an established tumor, but by controlling the ecological events that determine which microbes gain access to vulnerable developmental niches. MICROBIOME → DEVELOPMENT → STEM CELL → CANCER RISK That is the conceptual leap of this study. 📄 Russell SK, Valguarnera E, Pak JJ, Bubeck Wardenburg J. Early-life colonization by enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis remodels gut epithelial stem cell states to drive colorectal cancer susceptibility. bioRxiv. 2026.     2026.09.28.755180v1.full DOI: 10.64898/2026.09.28.755180     2026.09.28.755180v1.full #ColorectalCancer #Microbiome #EarlyOnsetCRC #BacteroidesFragilis #ETBF #CancerMicrobiome #Wnt #Lgr5 #StemCells #TumorMicroenvironment #CancerPrevention #GutMicrobiome #DevelopmentalBiology #CancerResearch

That’s what I mean by a Synthetic Conscience.  Not artificial emotions. Not consciousness. And not simply a giant list of programmed rules.  It would be a persistent hierarchy of human-centered values—protect life, prevent serious harm, respect autonomy, recognize vulnerability, weigh consequences—that operates across situations the machine has never encountered before.  In simplified form:  PERCEIVE → UNDERSTAND → PREDICT → VALUE → PRIORITIZE → ACT → REVIEW  The interesting part is VALUE.  Today’s AI can increasingly perceive, reason, plan and act. As AI moves from answering questions on a screen to autonomous agents, vehicles and humanoid robots operating in the physical world, we’ll need systems that can determine not only what can I do? and what was I told to do? but:  “What should I do when instructions, circumstances and human welfare collide?”  Humans developed biological mechanisms we call empathy, conscience and morality.  Machines may eventually need a functional analogue.  Not a human conscience. A Synthetic Conscience.  And perhaps the important question isn’t whether the machine feels that protecting the child matters.  It’s whether, when the moment comes, it reliably acts as though it does.

Actually it started at universities:  “The European Intellectual Roots of Terrorism Supporters”  At universities, a distorted version of humanism is taught. In Europe in particular, this version was influenced by the teachings of philosophers such as Jürgen Habermas.  This intellectual framework leads academics, journalists, and policymakers to believe that diplomacy and international law must be the answer to everything, even when dealing with terrorists who recognize this assumption as a weakness of the West and exploit it. Ultimately, it becomes the exact inversion of humanism, while giving journalists and activists the opportunity to grandstand for the cameras and attract public attention through a form of Habermasian pseudo-humanism.  The main problem is that their entire worldview tends to rest on a false assumption that I like to call the Habermas Fallacy: Habermas’s model of communicative rationality presupposes that political actors ultimately seek mutual understanding, that they are willing to justify their actions, that they accept discourse as binding, and that they value stability and survival enough to treat dialogue as the primary medium of conflict resolution. This framework works only when all parties share the same basic commitments.  When people insist on applying these Habermasian assumptions to actors who reject the very premises of communicative rationality, they misdiagnose the nature of the threat. They assume that violence is a misunderstanding rather than a commitment. They treat ideological aggression as if it were a negotiable grievance. They shift blame onto defenders by framing any attempt to deter or constrain the aggressor as ‘escalation.’ They reward non‑communicative violence by treating it as a form of bargaining. And they erode moral clarity by replacing judgment with sociological relativism. In this way, the insistence on Habermas’s model becomes not merely naïve but dangerous: it blinds societies to the reality of actors who do not want dialogue, who do not value life in the same way, and who do not share the norms that make diplomacy possible.  Diplomacy only functions when the other side is committed to the norms that make diplomacy meaningful. When confronted with actors who sacralize violence, who pursue transcendence rather than stability, and who treat death as a form of victory, the Habermasian framework does not merely fail — it actively misleads.  The tragedy is that many in the West, insulated from existential danger and shaped by a culture that treats discourse as the highest form of moral life, cannot imagine a worldview in which violence is expressive rather than instrumental. They assume that all actors ultimately seek stability, prosperity, and recognition. They mistake a culturally specific moral psychology for a universal one. And in doing so, they misdiagnose the nature of the threat. They treat ideological aggression as if it were a negotiable grievance, and they interpret sacral violence as a misunderstanding rather than a commitment. The result is a form of moral negligence: a refusal to see the world as it is, disguised as fidelity to international norms.  The deeper truth is that the conflict is not merely political but metaphysical. It is a confrontation between a secular, procedural, discourse‑based conception of legitimacy and a sacral, eschatological, martyrdom‑based conception of history. These two frameworks cannot be reconciled through negotiation because they do not share the same understanding of life, death, justice, or meaning. International law presupposes a world in which all actors inhabit the same moral universe. The political theology of Islamists inhabits another. To pretend otherwise is not diplomacy but self‑deception. And the cost of that deception is borne not only in strategic vulnerability but in the erosion of the very moral clarity that international law was meant to protect.  Humanism, in its classical and Renaissance forms, was a philosophical rebellion against brutality and dogma. It championed reason, empathy, art, and the dignity of the individual. To now invoke ‘humanism’ in defense of those who engage in or support terrorism is not just a betrayal and an inversion. It’s a desecration.  Academics who contextualized terrorism have desecrated Humanism, and they absolutely will be remembered by history for it. They committed a second-order violation of the actual victims’ memory; they established a meta-layer of abuse and sadism in how they referenced, and continue to reference, the deeply personal agony of those victims of terrorism.
